scope: Installed SynapseAI 1.24.1-482; binary implementation and CPU queries, not recovered public HAL C++ source; no REA; no accelerator jobs

consumer_chain.effect: HAL getSinglePortBw * getChipPortsNr(A/B) -> float PerfAttr offsets 0x24/0x34; no clock conversion
Normal branch sums QOR float offsets 0x24, 0x34, 0x44, 0x54 without clock conversion

unit_verdict: The traced software bandwidth interface uses GB/s (gigabytes per second), not bytes per cycle. This evidence comes from the Gaudi3 producer and common compiler consumer, not an explicit unit on the Gaudi2 getter.

gaudi2_application_caveat.meaning: The normal Gaudi2 memory-attribute callback is empty in this build. Do not claim the Gaudi3 bandwidth formula is an active Gaudi2 performance limit. Other consumers were not exhaustively excluded.

withdrawn_claims: Measured 1.64-1.67TB/s cannot rule out a 2.64TB/s theoretical peak: lower sustained throughput does not contradict a higher peak.
0.8TB/s per MME is not an established Gaudi2 silicon maximum or proven enforced cost-model limit.
PV logical A traffic near 1.6TB/s is consistent with an input bottleneck hypothesis but does not establish an independent physical A budget from this getter.
still_valid: Gaudi2 BF16 CPU geometry queries return per-MME A/B/C counts 4/4/4 and chip 8/8/8 in the 16 tested configurations.
Existing compiler output measurements 1.638/1.668TB/s chip are effective measured rates, not physical write-active counters.
External single-MME MME-to-SRAM 3.2TB/s remains unverified and has not been disproved by these measurements.
